subject: Maths
title: Percentage increase and decrease
subtitle: Percentages of Amounts · KS3 Maths
learning_objective: I can find a percentage increase or decrease and express a change as a percentage.

key_vocab.definition: A percentage change tells you how much something has gone up or down compared to the original amount, expressed as a percentage.

sections.title: Learning Objective
sections.content: I can find a percentage increase or decrease and express a change as a percentage.

sections.title: Key Words
sections.content: Percentage change -- A percentage change tells you how much something has gone up or down compared to the original amount, expressed as a percentage.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
Percentage change = (difference ÷ original) × 100. Always divide by the ORIGINAL value.
% change = &frac{change}{original} × 100
Divide by the starting value, not the new value

Key examples:
  ✓ 20 to 25: change = 5, % = 5/20 × 100 = 25%  (increase)
  ✓ 80 to 60: change = 20, % = 20/80 × 100 = 25%  (decrease)
  ✓ Always divide by the ORIGINAL amount  (key rule)
  ✗ 20 to 25: % change = 5/25 × 100 = 20%  (divided by new, not original)
  ✗ Change from 80 to 60 = 20%  (must divide by original (80))

sections.title: Worked Example
sections.content:
Example 1 – percentage increase
  A price goes from £40 to £52. Find the percentage increase.
  Change = 52 - 40 = 12
  % change = 12 ÷ 40 × 100
  = 30% increase
  = 30% increase
  (Divide the change by the original amount.)

Example 2 – percentage decrease
  A weight drops from 80 kg to 68 kg. Find the percentage decrease.
  Change = 80 - 68 = 12
  % change = 12 ÷ 80 × 100
  = 15% decrease
  = 15% decrease
  (Same formula, but the answer is a decrease.)

sections.title: Real-world percentage change
sections.content:

(b) Temperature drops from 20°C to 15°C
(c) Population grows from 4000 to 4500
(d) Price falls from £90 to £72

sections.content:

(b) 160 to 120
(c) £35 to £42
(d) 250 g to 200 g
(e) £1200 to £1350

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
✓ Percentage change = change ÷ original × 100
✗ From 20 to 25 is a 20% increase
✓ Always divide by the original (starting) value
✗ A change from 80 to 60 and 60 to 80 are the same percentage
✓ From 50 to 65 is 30% increase (15/50 × 100)
